U.S. equities opened mixed, with the Nasdaq Composite down approximately 0.05% at the opening bell while the S&P 500 and Dow posted modest gains. Technology shares lagged as oil rebounded and concerns about competition in the semiconductor industry resurfaced.

The most consequential development was the reversal in energy markets. Expectations of relief from a proposed Russia–Ukraine energy ceasefire gave way to renewed concerns following attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure and continuing Middle East tensions. Brent was reported near $106 per barrel, approximately 2% higher, increasing inflation concerns.

Elevated long-term rates and questions over AI infrastructure returns remain headwinds. The cash Treasury market was closed for Columbus Day, limiting direct yield confirmation.

The opening does not confirm a major bearish reversal, but weakens the case for an immediate continuation rally. Tuesday left Nasdaq and semiconductors in a fragile position: the Nasdaq Composite closed down 0.15%, while SOX lost more than 2%. Overnight conditions improved modestly. Reuters reported Nasdaq futures up 0.3%, S&P 500 futures up 0.2%, Samsung up 2.4%, SK Hynix up 0.8%, and TSMC up 1.4% in Asian trading. This is evidence of stabilization after the chip selloff, but not yet proof of a durable U.S. semiconductor reversal.

ASML's results strengthen the fundamental AI-capex case. The company raised its 2026 sales outlook, reported demand extending toward 2030, and said planned capacity may not fully satisfy customers in 2027–2028. ASML shares were up 1.8% in early European trading, helping the European technology sector gain 0.8%. The U.S. confirmation test is whether strength spreads across equipment, foundry, memory, and AI-infrastructure names rather than remaining concentrated in ASML.

The macro backdrop is mixed. Reuters reported the 10-year Treasury yield near 5.204%; a separate current-market report placed the 10-year around 5.19% and the 2-year near 4.795%. Long yields have eased from last week's peak, offering some valuation relief, but remain restrictive. VIX/VXN and reliable SOX breadth readings were not verified and are left unavailable.

Brent remains the clearest counterweight. Reuters reported Brent at $106.03–$106.27 as attacks on vessels in the Strait of Hormuz and further regional strikes sustained supply-risk concerns. Elevated oil raises the risk that energy inflation offsets easing bond yields and complicates the Fed outlook.

The directional setup is better than Tuesday's close but not yet bullish. A constructive upgrade requires a benign CPI response, contained yields, Nasdaq gains that hold, and broad SOX participation. A hot CPI print, renewed yield pressure, or a narrow ASML-led bounce that fades would restore the bearish continuation case.

Market overview and semiconductor assessment: Reuters reported Nasdaq Composite at 26,988.31, down 0.78%, at 10:09 ET. NVDA fell 1.7%, MU 1%, and Intel 2.6%; Nasdaq decliners outnumbered advancers 3.3 to one. This suggests weak participation beyond a single heavyweight. Macro and liquidity: The official September CPI release showed headline inflation of 0.6% month over month and 3.7% year over year, with core inflation at 0.3% and 2.6%, respectively. Gasoline rose 9.1%, while shelter rose 0.4%. Energy drove much of the increase, but underlying inflation also remained firm. Our assessment is that this weakens the case for immediate valuation relief in growth stocks.

IBD reported the 10-year Treasury yield near 5.28% in early trading. That is a separate observation, not a synchronized reading with the Nasdaq figure. Falling technology shares alongside rising long yields supports a cautious interpretation of the CPI response. An early-market 2-year yield and synchronized VIX/VXN readings could not be verified after alternative-source searches and remain null. Overnight readings are not substituted.

Fundamentals, catalysts and risks: ASML's official results reported EUR11.7 billion in quarterly sales and EUR5.0 billion in net income, with full-year sales guidance of EUR44–45 billion. That provides supportive company evidence, but earnings strength alone does not establish improving semiconductor breadth. The key test is whether equipment strength spreads to foundry, memory and AI leaders, including TSM, AMD and AVGO; their checkpoint prices remain unverified.

Brent was around $106.30 in StoneX's pre-CPI commentary. This is background evidence of energy pressure, not a verified early-market quote. Persistent expensive oil remains an inflation risk; the actual intraday Brent reading is null.

Bias: Cautious / Negative. Confidence: Moderate. Event risk: High. This is our interpretation of the available evidence. Compared with the archived pre-market thesis, anticipated semiconductor stabilization has not received convincing opening confirmation, while inflation and yields have become less supportive. Missing SOX and QQQ observations limit confidence in the precise strength of the move.

Major events to watch: Today's Beige Book may clarify business pricing, employment and demand conditions. Tomorrow's PPI and retail-sales releases create another macro test; MarketWatch confirms both at 08:30 ET. Their outcomes remain unknown.

Confirmation conditions: A bullish reassessment requires Nasdaq and QQQ to recover and hold their opening range, broader semiconductor participation, and easing yield pressure. A bearish confirmation would be fresh intraday lows accompanied by persistent semiconductor weakness and rising yields. These are conditions to monitor, not observations already established.

Semiconductors remain the weak link. SOX was 11,242.58, down 3.78%, at 10:06:27 ET, substantially underperforming both Nasdaq benchmarks. Its observed morning range was 11,171.53–11,406.38. These are earlier morning observations, not verified 10:30 yields. Volatility and oil. VIX was 17.57 (+4.15%) at 09:48:31 ET and VXN 24.99 (+10.09%) at 09:59:46 ET, converting the source’s displayed GMT−5 times to New York daylight time. By midday, the market had escaped the opening semiconductor washout, but the recovery was becoming narrower and less convincing.

SOX stood at 11,334.36, up 0.16%, at 1:00 PM ET, according to MarketWatch. That was a sharp improvement from the 2.4% opening decline, but weaker than the 0.5% gain reported at 10:29 AM. The wider market was recovering as Brent retreated from its morning high and weak housing data pulled long Treasury yields lower. That eased the two most immediate valuation pressures on growth stocks: energy-driven inflation and expensive financing. The benefit to Nasdaq was incomplete, however, because investors continued rotating toward healthcare, financials and smaller companies while questioning the returns on debt-funded AI infrastructure. [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/global-markets-global-markets-2026-10-20/) [Business Insider](https://www.businessinsider.com/ai-elice-ipo-cloud-chip-stocks-mu-nvda-wdc-2026-10)

The semiconductor recovery therefore looked tactical rather than fundamental. The collapse of South Korea’s Elice listing and weakness in Asian memory shares kept attention on AI spending quality. Without synchronized checkpoint prices for NVDA, AMD, AVGO, MU and TSM, there is not enough evidence to claim that the key U.S. leaders were confirming SOX’s rebound.

The afternoon test was straightforward: SOX needed to hold above Monday’s 11,316.34 close and rebuild breadth while Nasdaq resisted the pull from weaker mega-cap communication-services stocks. A failure to hold that level would turn an impressive opening reversal into another failed bounce.

### What changed since the previous session

At 10:29 AM, SOX was up 0.5% with 21 of 30 components advancing after an opening collapse. At 1:00 PM it was still positive, but the gain had narrowed to 0.16%. Oil and yields were becoming less hostile, yet semiconductor momentum was fading. The signal therefore shifted from “opening reversal” to “reversal under confirmation.”

Weak guidance or heavy capital needs would intensify the market’s financing concerns before Meta and Tesla report Wednesday.

The bearish scenario is a renewed SOX break below Monday’s close, followed by pressure on QQQ and the major chip leaders. That would confirm that the morning move was short-covering inside a damaged trend rather than the start of sustained accumulation.

**Overall assessment:** Stabilization is present, but momentum and breadth are not yet strong enough to upgrade the Nasdaq outlook. The correct stance remains neutral–cautious until semiconductor leadership persists through the afternoon.

NasDecode Pre-Market Analysis

Wednesday, October 21, 2026 · 00:30 ET scheduled checkpoint

Nasdaq bias

**Neutral–constructive / earnings-dependent**

Confidence

Event risk

## Market overview

Nasdaq’s central tension is whether improving AI demand can outweigh the cost of financing it while semiconductor leadership remains unconfirmed.

Tuesday’s close left that question open. The Nasdaq Composite finished almost unchanged at 26,424.82, and QQQ slipped 0.10% to $717.63, even as value, healthcare and small caps advanced. SOX recovered sharply from its intraday low but still closed lower on Nasdaq’s official index page; NVDA, AMD, AVGO and MU declined, while TSM was the only monitored chip leader to finish positive. The tape avoided a broad risk-off break, but the support came from rotation rather than renewed AI leadership. [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/nasdaq-futures-dip-oil-prices-climb-earnings-loom-2026-10-20/) · [Nasdaq SOX](https://indexes.nasdaq.com/Index/History/SOX)

SpaceX’s after-close results strengthened the demand side of the AI argument but also sharpened the capital-intensity risk. The company reported $14.6 billion of quarterly revenue, up 161%, with AI revenue at $7.6 billion; capital expenditure reached $19.6 billion, of which $16.4 billion went to AI infrastructure. That is direct evidence that compute demand is translating into revenue, but not that the industry’s expanding investment burden will produce uniformly attractive returns. [SEC filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1181412/000162828026066482/spaceexplorationtechnologi.htm) · [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/spacex-quarterly-revenue-jumps-beats-estimates-ai-business-surges-2026-10-20/)

Netflix added a more restrained message. Third-quarter revenue met its forecast and operating margin exceeded it, but full-year revenue guidance moved slightly below the midpoint of the prior range because advertising rollout was slower than expected. Together, the two releases reward proven monetization and penalize spending or execution that outruns it. [Netflix filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1065280/000106528026000290/ex991_q326.htm)

Later overnight evidence—not available at the 00:30 checkpoint—was more constructive for risk appetite: Reuters reported S&P 500 e-mini futures up 0.4%, Tesla up 1.3% premarket, and broad gains in Japan and South Korea. Yet Brent had risen to $110.40 by 02:30 ET on Middle East supply concerns, restoring an inflation risk that could limit how far lower yields and better earnings lift long-duration technology. Exact Nasdaq futures and synchronized chip premarket prices remain unavailable. [Global markets](https://www.reuters.com/world/china/global-markets-view-europe-2026-10-21/) · [Oil](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/oil-rises-middle-east-supply-worries-2026-10-21/)

The decisive events are after the close. Meta and Tesla must show that AI, advertising, automotive and energy investment can produce cash returns without another destabilizing increase in capital needs. With no major U.S. macro release on MarketWatch’s Wednesday calendar, company guidance and oil are more likely than scheduled data to set the next Nasdaq direction. [MarketWatch calendar](https://www.marketwatch.com/economy-politics/calendar)

[Treasury](https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value=2026) |
| VIX / VXN | Tuesday displayed readings: 17.31 / 25.22. Source timestamp was 15:15:01 GMT−5; exact ET interpretation and 00:30 readings are **unavailable**. [VIX](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/VIX:INDEXCBOE) · [VXN](https://www.google.com/finance/quote/VXN:INDEXCBOE) |
| Brent | $109.64 at 00:22 GMT, or 20:22 ET Tuesday—before the checkpoint. Later $110.40 at 06:30 GMT, or 02:30 ET, up 1.5%. [Reuters](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/oil-rises-middle-east-supply-worries-2026-10-21/) |
| Asian chips: later context | After the checkpoint, AP reported KOSPI +3.3%, Nikkei +0.9% and Taiwan’s Taiex +1.3%; Samsung and SK Hynix led Korea’s rebound. Exact official constituent breadth and individual observation times are **unavailable**. [AP](https://apnews.com/article/4fa93685cd49e51e7ff0d840fdd38b0d) |

## What to Watch Today

1. **Meta Q3 results, after the close; call at 16:30 ET.** Meta is the clearest test of whether AI improves advertising economics fast enough to justify large infrastructure commitments. Strong engagement, revenue and free-cash-flow evidence with controlled spending would support Nasdaq and semiconductor suppliers. A capex increase without faster monetization would reinforce the financing concern. [Meta Investor Relations](https://investor.atmeta.com/investor-news/press-release-details/2026/Meta-to-Announce-Third-Quarter-2026-Results/default.aspx)

2. **Tesla Q3 results, after the close; call at 17:30 ET.** Investors need evidence that deliveries translate into margins and cash flow while AI and energy projects remain financeable. Better automotive economics and credible growth in autonomy or storage would help high-beta Nasdaq sentiment; weak margins or spending-heavy guidance would hurt it. Speculation about a SpaceX transaction is not a substitute for operating evidence. [Tesla Investor Relations](https://ir.tesla.com/press-release/tesla-third-quarter-2026-production-deliveries-and-deployments)

3. **SOX participation at the cash open.** The constructive outcome requires SOX to reclaim 11,316.34, Monday’s close, with NVDA, AMD, AVGO, MU and TSM participating together. A rebound led only by TSM or one mega-cap would remain fragile. A break below Tuesday’s 11,043.24 low would confirm that the late recovery failed.

4. **Brent and Middle East supply risk.** Oil holding below Tuesday’s $111.99 high would keep the inflation impulse contained. A renewed push above that level would raise the risk of higher yields and compress technology valuations, even if earnings remain sound.

## NasDecode interpretation

The constructive case is no longer based only on promises of future AI demand: SpaceX supplied strong revenue evidence, and later Asian trading showed renewed appetite for memory and semiconductor exposure. Confirmation still requires U.S. chips to broaden, QQQ to reclaim $722.75 and SOX to recover 11,316.34 without Brent or the 10-year yield breaking higher.

The bearish case strengthens if investors focus on the $19.6 billion spending burden rather than the revenue acceleration, especially if Meta adds another capex surprise. QQQ below $710.39 or SOX below 11,043.24, combined with Brent above $111.99 or the 10-year yield above 5.15%, would reconnect earnings risk, financing pressure and energy inflation.

**Overall assessment:** The setup is neutral–constructive but highly earnings-dependent. AI demand is increasingly visible; broad U.S. semiconductor confirmation is not.
